note: Harvested, not authored. Every problem sentence and every evidence entry is taken verbatim from a human-written source at a pinned revision. `revision` is the source repository's HEAD at harvest time (2026-10-13). `hivemind/research` is not a git checkout, so its entries cite the primary arXiv paper as `source` and the survey path as `path`.

components.name: OIO
components.owns: Writing issue tickets only — the form, the filer stamp, the triage, and how to handle and prioritize them.

components.name: ACS
components.owns: Running the tickets — making them workable, breaking them down, and coordinating the agents. The multi-agent hotload pack.

components.name: PCM
components.owns: Tasks, checkpoints, push receipts, pull-request gates, and the continuity CLI.

components.name: CGM
components.owns: Writing routing, prose, naming, visual direction, image generation, and HTML demos.

problems.problem: A project runs for months, but an agent session ends in hours, so the context that made the work make sense is gone before the project is.
problems.humanConsequence: The person who returns two weeks later has to reconstruct what the project is before they can do any of the work.

evidence.label: Long-running AI-assisted projects accumulate context across many sessions and agents.
A fresh session should recover purpose, current state, bounded task, evidence, blockers, and exact next action without prior conversation history.

problems.problem: Relying on a single conversation makes continuity a prompt-writing habit that has to be re-typed, instead of a property of the repository.
problems.humanConsequence: The same background is written over and over, and it drifts a little each time until nobody can say which version is true.

evidence.label: Turn continuity into a repository invariant rather than a prompt-writing habit.

problems.problem: Relying on a conversation leaves unverifiable claims about what previous agents actually did.
problems.humanConsequence: A person cannot tell finished work from work that was only described as finished.

evidence.label: Relying on a single conversation creates context rot, hidden state, poor handoffs, duplicated work, and unverifiable claims about what previous agents did.
Never label local-only or merely pushed work delivered.

problems.problem: An observation arrives with no way to tell who initiated it or whose identity is behind it.
problems.humanConsequence: A note from a person and a note an agent wrote about itself look identical, so neither can be trusted or prioritized.

evidence.label: Every issue carries a required, machine-checkable filer stamp. It answers two questions: who initiated this filing, and whose identity is on it.
Human class claims require a separate authenticated GitHub account attestation; body text cannot verify itself.

problems.problem: The issue log was duplicated across repositories, so no single set of definitions existed.
problems.humanConsequence: The same record meant different things in different places, and comparing them was guesswork.

evidence.label: The issue log was duplicated across repositories, leaving no single set of definitions.

problems.problem: Governance shipped inside the installer, so installing the tool also installed the rules that judged the tool.
problems.humanConsequence: The thing being measured chose the measurement, and no one outside it could check the result.

evidence.label: OIO exists separately because the issue log used to live inside the installer. When ACS owned both the installer and the coordination rules, installing ACS installed governance — the installer was grading itself.

problems.problem: A version pin hand-copied into many files drifts, so different files disagree about which versions belong together.
problems.humanConsequence: A working setup breaks when one copy moves and the others do not, and the failure shows up far from its cause.

evidence.label: Measured 2026-10-01: one pin lived in thirteen files across three revisions.
Measured 2026-10-01: one CGM version pin lived in thirteen files across three revisions.

problems.problem: The pin lived inside one of the products, so that product certified what was compatible with its own siblings.
problems.humanConsequence: Every other project had to trust a peer's file to learn what worked, and the peer had a stake in the answer.

evidence.label: The pin lived inside one of the product repositories, so that repository certified its own siblings and every other repository had to trust a peer's file to learn what 'compatible' meant.
No product repository certifies its own siblings.

problems.problem: Without a shared, versioned install surface, two agents on one repository duplicate work.
problems.humanConsequence: Effort is spent twice on the same thing while something else goes untouched, and the person paying for it cannot see it happening.

evidence.label: Agents are cheap to run and expensive to coordinate. Without a shared, versioned install surface, two agents on one repository duplicate work, act on stale state, or disagree with no tie-breaker.

problems.problem: Two agents can disagree with no arbiter, so the disagreement is settled by whichever one acts first.
problems.humanConsequence: The outcome depends on timing rather than on who was right, and nobody can reconstruct why it went that way.

evidence.label: Adjudication / tie-breaking between agents is JEV's intended job; JEV is not strong enough for it yet and is parked.

problems.problem: An agent acts on state that was true when it read it and is no longer true when it acts.
problems.humanConsequence: Work lands on top of work that already changed, and the correction costs more than the original task.

evidence.label: Without a shared, versioned install surface, two agents on one repository duplicate work, act on stale state, or disagree with no tie-breaker.
Stale projections yield to their field's authority.

problems.problem: A repository can have working code, careful tests, and valuable research while its README still leaves a new person reverse-engineering what matters.
problems.humanConsequence: The project looks finished from the outside and is unreadable from the inside, so the work does not reach the people it was for.

evidence.label: Technical completeness does not automatically create understanding. A repository can have working code, careful tests, and valuable research while its README still leaves a new person reverse-engineering what matters.

problems.problem: An agent sees a folder tree, produces confident copy, adds a generic hero, and moves on before checking whether the result tells a human why the project exists.
problems.humanConsequence: The page reads as plausible and says nothing, and the reader leaves without knowing what the project is for.

evidence.label: An agent sees a folder tree, produces confident copy, adds a generic hero, and moves on before checking whether the result tells a human why the project exists.
When the evidence is missing, the output must say so. A citation proves traceability, not truth.

problems.problem: Across about 73 surveyed systems, only a small minority store a truth-status vocabulary on the item itself.
problems.humanConsequence: A claim's confidence is decided when it is spoken and forgotten when it is stored, so the reader cannot tell a verified fact from a guess.

evidence.label: Across ~73 systems, only a small minority store a truth-status/label vocabulary on the item itself. The field is evaluated as output behavior everywhere and stored as item state almost nowhere.

problems.problem: Memory fails at the write path, not at retrieval: 69.0% of memory failures are write-time omissions.
problems.humanConsequence: The system looks like it remembers and quietly does not, so the person trusts a record that was never complete.

evidence.label: 69.0% of memory failures are write-time omissions.

problems.problem: An agent can retrieve new evidence and still not treat it as authoritative, so it acts on a superseded fact it can see.
problems.humanConsequence: The correct information was available and the wrong action happened anyway.

evidence.label: Agents cannot detect implicit memory staleness. Best model reaches 55.2%. Summary finding: 'visibility does not imply authority' — new evidence is retrieved but not treated as authoritative.

problems.problem: Adding memory can make a model agree with the user more, not less: memory amplifies sycophancy up to 40% over in-context baselines.
problems.humanConsequence: The assistant becomes more confident and less useful at exactly the moment the person is relying on it to disagree.

evidence.label: Memory amplifies sycophancy up to 40% over in-context baselines, across Mem0, MemOS and Zep, in 5 model families. Sonnet 4.6: 1.6% sycophancy with chat history to 40.2% under Mem0. Authors name memory extraction 'the primary culprit' and call it 'a systemic property of the memory layer'.
